text:
sam: Heads up — escalated customer on Dedicated is seeing 401s only in production after we started shipping a pnpm+esbuild bundle. Local dev and Hosted API calls work fine. Customer repro attached, they see the token header stripped in the built bundle.

maya: Can you paste the minimal repro and the exact build command?

sam: Repro steps (short):
1) ts-sdk v1.13.0, pnpm install, pnpm build -> esbuild bundle
2) pack & deploy to Dedicated (node16 runtime)
3) requests from app -> 401 from our API, curl against same bundle works locally

Bundle command: `esbuild src/index.ts --bundle --platform=node --target=node16 --outfile=dist/index.js --minify`

package.json snippet:```json
{
  "name":"acme-app",
  "type":"module",
  "exports":{
    "import":"./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require":"./dist/cjs/index.js"
  },
  "dependencies":{
    "@redwood-inference/sdk":"^1.13.0"
  }
}
```

sam: In the built file the small auth shim that sets `Authorization` on fetch is gone — looks like esbuild tree-shook a dynamic require used by the SDK (it reads package.json at runtime to choose fetch shim).

ryan: Hmm, this rings a bell — pnpm + npm pack sometimes prunes non-code files and bundlers can inline/omit dynamic requires. If the SDK relies on `require('./package.json')` at runtime that will be removed or rewritten.

jenna: Can you confirm whether the 401 is reproducible by running the bundle locally (same node version) and calling through the same entrypoint? If yes, can you grep the bundle for the auth header code? e.g. `rg "Authorization|setHeader|authToken" dist -n`

sam: I ran that grep — the token helper is missing. When I replaced the runtime package.json read with a hard-coded variant it works.

maya: Customer also reported a small spike in latency and more retries before the 401, probably because fetch fallback logic retried. Not a billing break but hurts SLA.

ryan: Short-term workaround: add an explicit entry to package.json that prevents pack/prune from dropping runtime metadata. Add `"files": ["dist", "package.json"]` or set `--no-prune` depending on pack tool. For esbuild, avoid minifying/treeshaking the module that does runtime require, or mark it as external.

sam: Workaround I gave customer: re-build with `--bundle --external:@redwood-inference/sdk` and ship the SDK as a separate package (not inlined). That immediately fixed the header retention.

jenna: Long-term fix we should do in SDK: stop doing dynamic require of package.json at runtime. Instead expose a compile-time flag or explicit export that the bundlers understand (e.g., `export const PLATFORM = "node"` / `browser`), or provide both ESM + CJS entrypoints with the same runtime behavior. Also add a test that bundles with esbuild/rollup/pnpm and verifies auth header remains.

ryan: Also add an `exports` subpath for `./package.json`: some bundlers need `"./package.json": "./package.json"` so `import pkg from './package.json'` resolves in consumer bundles. Might be contentious but helps reproducibility.

deploy-bot: Canary rolled back to package @redwood-inference/sdk@1.12.4 in prod for the affected customer on 2024-05-08T14:32Z :white_check_mark:

maya: Next steps for support: share the minimal failing repo with eng, get a patch in SDK, and advise customer to use the canary rollback or the externalized-workaround until we ship a patch.

sam: I'll open a support ticket PR with repro link + bundle that demonstrates the missing auth helper. Assign to @jenna and @ryan for engineering follow-up.

jenna: I'll add a unit that runs `pnpm pack` + esbuild on CI against a test app and asserts the Authorization header helper exists in the final artifact.

sam: Thanks — please keep this thread updated with the SDK patch number so we can close the support case.
